claims.text: Elevated-temperature degradation of additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 is governed primarily by synergistic oxidation of Cr and Ti.
In oxidizing atmospheres, Cr and Ti rapidly form a continuous mixed Cr/Ti oxide layer.
The mixed Cr/Ti oxide layer protects the underlying fcc matrix.
Reducing atmospheres suppress oxidation and prevent sufficient external oxide formation.
Insufficient external oxide formation under reducing conditions enhances internal oxidation and localized matrix degradation.
The as-manufactured alloy is a homogeneous fcc-phase material.
The as-manufactured alloy contains minimal pre-existing oxide.
The starting alloy retains high strength and fatigue performance.
Cr and Ti diffusion kinetics within the fcc matrix mediate oxide-scale formation and internal oxidation.
Cr and Ti segregate to the surface or internal grain boundaries during exposure.
Cr and Ti preferentially oxidize under oxidizing conditions.
The proposed Cr/Ti-rich scale is continuous and adherent and acts as a barrier to further degradation.
Reducing exposure causes elemental depletion near the alloy surface.
Reducing exposure promotes internal oxidation and microstructural degradation.
Oxidizing exposure will preserve mechanical integrity relative to reducing exposure.
Internal oxidation under reducing exposure will correlate with reduced localized material properties.
The proposed mechanism applies over approximately 700–900°C and exposure durations around 50 hours.
Outside the proposed temperature and duration limits, phase transformations or other degradation modes may dominate.

contradictions.description: Reducing conditions are said to suppress or inhibit oxidation while simultaneously enhancing internal oxidation. This could be coherent only if a residual oxygen activity permits selective internal oxidation while preventing an external scale, but that necessary condition is not specified.
